text:
Ashley (support): AcmeCorp just reported a spike of 502s + timeouts hitting /v1/generate (model=redwood-13b-v1 hosted). Started ~2024-11-03T09:12:00Z, observed ~18% error rate across requests. Customer impacted in production, traffic ~120rps. Escalating to eng-oncall.

Ajay (eng-oncall): on it. Any recent deploys or config changes in the last hour? need request ids and a sample of the 502 body if possible.

Ashley (support): deploy-bot shows a canary rolled at 2024-11-03T08:58:22Z for redwood-13b-v1-beta. Attaching a short log sample:```[2024-11-03T09:11:43Z] req=acme-req-1298 gateway: upstream=runtime timeout status=502
[2024-11-03T09:11:44Z] req=acme-req-1302 runtime: kv-cache-stall duration=234ms
[2024-11-03T09:11:44Z] req=acme-req-1302 runtime: error="batcher overflow"
```

deploy-bot: Canary redwood-13b-v1-beta deployed to canary pool (id: canary-42) at 2024-11-03T08:58:22Z.

sre-bot: Alert triggered: hosted-inference-503-rate > threshold for customer AcmeCorp (avg error 17.9% over 5m).

Jordan (runtime): seeing repeated batcher queue spikes for canary pool. backlog spikes coincide with longer prompts and ~2x token lengths for AcmeCorp traffic. When queue > 256 we start dropping requests -> 502.

Lee (infra): didn't touch gateway configs. I can check autoscaler and pool capacity. Can we temporarily shift AcmeCorp to a stable model variant or route to dedicated-sized pool?

Ajay (eng-oncall): mitigation plan: 1) route AcmeCorp to redwood-7b-v1 fallback via routing policy; 2) disable canary pool for new traffic for 10m; 3) increase batcher concurrency limit + restart batcher workers in canary pool. Doing 1 now.

Ajay (eng-oncall): routing rule applied: tenant=acmecorp -> model=redwood-7b-v1 (fallback). Confirming lower error rate on metrics. :white_check_mark:

Ashley (support): customer notified: "We routed you to a fallback model to stabilize requests while we investigate. ETA 2h for full resolution." Customer replied: "thanks, keep us posted".

Jordan (runtime): repro steps I used: ```for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":1200}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done``` This reproduces queue growth on canary. Observed logs: `batcher overflow` -> downstream 502.

Lee (infra): autoscaler for canary pool was not scaling up due to a bug in the capacity-checker that ignores ephemeral quota for canary pools. Patching now to respect ephemeral headroom.

Ajay (eng-oncall): temporary hotfix: increased batcher limit from 256 -> 384 and restarted canary batcher. After restart queueing reduced and error spikes stopped for non-Acme traffic.

Jordan (runtime): root cause hypothesis: canary model variant introduced a slight perf regression (longer per-token latency) combined with unhandled batcher backpressure -> queue saturation -> gateway 502s for affected tenant traffic.

Maria (customer-success): customer flagged billing concerns if fallback reduces quality. I told them we'll log quality change and coordinate a test window. They want a postmortem and SLA credit if we caused >0.5% errors for >30m.

Ajay (eng-oncall): immediate action items: - route back only after stability verification (Ajay) - create postmortem ticket with timeline (Ashley) - patch capacity-checker (Lee) - perf regression triage for canary model (Jordan) - notify billing & legal for potential SLA credit (Maria).

Ashley (support): created ticket INC-2024-1147 and started a Loom with timeline. Ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2024-1147

Lee (infra): raised PR to fix capacity-checker: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/567 (hotfix branch). Planning canary deploy of fix in 15m.

Jordan (runtime): pinned canary to older runtime-simd kernel for redwood-13b-v1-beta to measure perf delta. Will post perf numbers in ~30m.

Ajay (eng-oncall): status check: error rate for AcmeCorp after fallback: 0.6% over last 5m (was 18%). Other customers stable. Marking mitigation as effective.

Maria (customer-success): customer asked for roll-forward plan: prefer full revert of canary until regression is fixed. Will coordinate with account team.

Ajay (eng-oncall): agreed. Rolling back canary for redwood-13b-v1-beta from canary pool now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed for redwood-13b-v1-beta at 2024-11-03T10:02:15Z.

Ashley (support): handing off to postmortem. War room summary: brief outage-like impact to single tenant due to canary perf regression + batcher backpressure + autoscaler bug. Mitigated by routing fallback + batcher bump + canary rollback. Customer routed to fallback, notified.

Ajay (eng-oncall): next-day postmortem owners and due dates: root cause triage (Jordan) due 2024-11-05, infra hotfix verification (Lee) due 2024-11-04, customer follow-up & SLA assessment (Maria) due 2024-11-04, postmortem doc (Ashley) due 2024-11-05. I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

Ashley (support): thanks all — closing war room thread and moving to postmortem doc. If anything new pops up ping @ajay.

Ajay (eng-oncall): closing checks: metrics stable, no regression in other tenants. Adding follow-up checklist to INC-2024-1147.

Maria (customer-success): customer confirmed they are back to acceptable error rates and want a scheduled review before canary re-introduction.

Jordan (runtime): leaving a short note in postmortem draft: investigate batching heuristics for long-token prompts and add tenant-specific backpressure thresholds.

Lee (infra): will monitor canary pools and autoscaler metrics for next 24h.

Ashley (support): archive this war room, moving actions to ticket. :file_cabinet:
